content.text: Logic talks about propositions, sets and numbers. Do such things exist?

content.definition: Abstract objects exist independently of minds and language. We discover them.
Abstract objects do not really exist. Talk of them is a useful way of speaking.

examples.title: The puzzle
lines: Numbers have no place in space or time.
We cannot touch them or see them.
Yet we seem to know facts about them.
examples.note: How could we know about things we never meet?

examples.title: Two answers
lines: Platonist: 2 + 2 = 4 was true before anyone counted.
Nominalist: it is true of how counting works, with no number objects needed.

question.prompt: What does a Platonist say about abstract objects?
options: They do not exist at all
They exist only in our minds
question.hint: Platonists say we discover them rather than invent them.
question.explanation: Platonists hold that numbers and propositions exist independently of any mind or language.
